ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The flower-lifting and smile scene names the paired actions attributed to the Buddha and Kashyapa; later masters quote, judge, and sometimes reject the scene’s inherited formulation.
EvidenceBody: The flower-sermon scene: Shakyamuni Buddha holds up a flower before the Vulture Peak assembly, the assembly is at a loss, and Kashyapa smiles . The compact phrase joins two different actors' gestures; it does not say that one person both holds the flower and smiles. The recorded Buddha then entrusts Kashyapa with the treasury of the true teaching eye and a transmission outside teachings. Later masters challenge the scene. Yuelin Zongshan assigns thirty blows at the moment of the flower and smile. Dongshan Shouchu says people know the compact phrase but do not know the World-Honored One. Yulin Tongxiu calls it a single transmission and says it has made clear-eyed people laugh. Zhongfeng Mingben says that if the great affair were exhausted by such gestures, holding up the flower and smiling and cutting off an arm to settle the mind would be mere plays. Tianran Hanshi calls only this purport real and all other verbal teachings false, then immediately warns against making it a fixed reality. Zen defines the invoked Buddha and Kashyapa through this public scene, entrustment, and later examinations rather than through general hagiography.
